t: Ruben's revolt against Byzantium in 1080 founded the principality; Levon II's coronation at Tarsus on 6 January 1198, backed by the Holy Roman Emperor, made it a kingdom.
Het'um I's alliance with the Mongols, sealed at Karakorum in 1250 and 1253, drew Mamluk vengeance: Sis was sacked in 1266 and 40,000 Armenians carried off.
Cilician society adopted Western feudalism, chivalry and French titles, and the Armenian alphabet gained two letters, Ֆ and Օ, from the contact.
dyk: Marco Polo set out on his journey to China in 1271 from Ayas, the Cilician Armenian port where the Genoese held licensed warehouses and Italian was the language of trade.
ev: Ruben, a noble close to the murdered Bagratid king Gagik II, raises Armenian troops against the Byzantine Empire and founds the principality of Cilicia.
Prince Levon II is crowned King Levon I in the cathedral of Tarsus on 6 January, with a banner from Henry VI, Holy Roman Emperor; Cilician Armenia becomes a kingdom.
Queen Zabel is forced to marry Het'um, son of the regent Constantine of Baberon; as Het'um I he unites the rival Rubenid and Het'umid houses.
Het'um I visits Möngke Khan at Karakorum, confirming the Armeno-Mongol alliance his brother Smbat negotiated in 1247–1250.
Mamluk forces under Al-Mansur Ali and Qalawun overrun the Armenians at the Disaster of Mari, sack and burn Sis, massacre thousands and take 40,000 captives.
Het'um II joins the Mongol khan Ghazan to defeat the Mamluks at the Battle of Wadi al-Khazandar on 23 December.
The Mongol representative Bularghu murders King Levon III, the former king Het'um II and their party outside Anazarba; Oshin drives him out and becomes king.
Sis falls to the Mamluks, then the fortress of Gaban where King Levon V had taken refuge; the kingdom ends and Levon dies in exile in Paris in 1393.

f.capital: Tarsus, then Sis (moved by Thoros I, c. 1100)
f.founder: Ruben, who founded the Rubenid principality in 1080; Levon I, crowned the first king on 6 January 1198
f.predecessor: Byzantine Cilicia and the principality of Philaretos Brachamios (1078–1085), settled by refugees from Bagratid Armenia
f.successor: The Mamluk Sultanate (conquest of 1375); the royal title passed to James I of Cyprus in 1396
